summary:
ARTEMIS BASE CAMP is an interactive lunar-outpost simulator designed to introduce children aged 7–12 to the challenges of living and working on the Moon. Players take on the role of junior astronauts during an eight-Sol mission near the lunar South Pole. They explore a 3D lunar environment, operate a rover, complete engineering tasks, respond to mission emergencies, and make decisions that affect the outpost’s power, life support, food, and radiation protection systems.

The project turns complex space-engineering concepts into an accessible, hands-on learning experience. By showing how resources and systems depend on one another, it encourages curiosity, problem-solving, and an understanding of the challenges future lunar explorers will face.
details:
ARTEMIS BASE CAMP is a browser-based lunar mission simulator set near the Moon’s South Pole. Players explore a three-dimensional outpost, switch between astronauts, operate a rover, collect lunar ice, and complete interactive engineering tasks. During an eight-Sol mission, they must respond to emergencies and make decisions that affect the colony’s power, life support, radiation protection, and food systems.

The project is designed to make space exploration understandable through interaction rather than lengthy explanations. Its benefits include developing problem-solving skills, encouraging scientific curiosity, and helping young learners understand how different systems work together to support human life beyond Earth.

The project was developed as a standalone web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Its creative approach combines exploration, resource management, mini-games, and mission events in one learning experience. The design considers the needs of younger players, including accessible tasks, clear feedback, and engaging gameplay.
